mainTopic: Presumed childlessness, כתובה claims, and who is believed about infertility
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point. The laws of וסת and שור המועד each need three times to set a pattern, which matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Then a ברייתא rules that a woman who had no children with two husbands may marry a third only if he already has children. If she marries a man without children, she leaves without a כתובה. The גמרא asks whether the earlier husbands can take back their כתובה money if the third marriage is also childless. It answers no, because she can say she only became weak now. It also asks whether she can claim her כתובה from the third husband after having children with a fourth. רב פפא rejects the first answer, which could make the גט void, and says instead that she only became healthy now. Finally, when husband and wife blame each other for having no children, רבי אמי rules that she is believed, because only she can know. רבי אמי and רבא then disagree about whether a man may marry another wife without divorcing the first.

steps.title: Menstrual patterns and the goring ox need three times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes showing that the laws of וסתות and שור המועד follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a pattern is set only after three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman does not set a menstrual pattern for herself until she has set it three times. She is not freed from that pattern until it has been broken three times. And for a forewarned ox, as we learned in a משנה: an ox does not become מועד until witnesses testify that it gored three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier point. It shows two known laws where a pattern needs three times, which matches the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא said that וסתות and שור המועד follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who requires three times for a חזקה. Here it brings the actual sources. A וסת is set by three times and removed by three times, and an ox becomes מועד only after three gorings. These are both clear cases where three times creates the pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's regular pattern of when her period comes
Is uprooted or broken (the pattern stops)
An ox known to gore, so its owner pays full damages
As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: וסת and שור המועד both need three times to set a pattern. This matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view on חזקה.

phrases.english: [A woman does not] establish a set pattern for herself,
until she has established it three times.
And she is not freed from the set pattern
until it is uprooted from her three times.
And the forewarned ox, as we learned in a משנה:
An ox does not become forewarned
until witnesses testify about it three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier claim (from the previous page) that וסתות and שור המועד follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.raayaObject: That וסתות and שור המועד follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (three times for a חזקה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about setting and uprooting a וסת, and the משנה in בבא קמא about an ox becoming מועד.

steps.title: A woman childless with two husbands must marry a man who has children
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that after two childless marriages, a woman may marry only a man who already has children. If she marries a man without children, she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If she married a first husband and had no children, and a second and had no children, she may marry a third only if he already has children. If she married a man who has no children, she is divorced without a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new rule. Two childless marriages make her presumed unable to have children, so she should marry only a man who has already done פריה ורביה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two failed marriages are enough to create a presumption here. This fits the view that a חזקה is set by two times. Because of that presumption, a man without children who marries her made a mistaken marriage. So she gets no כתובה when they divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: The money promised to a wife if the marriage ends

steps.confusionAlert: This rule sets the presumption after only two marriages, not three. Don't mix it up with the three-times cases in the step before.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the base case for both questions that come next.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: נִיסֵּת לָרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא הָיוּ לָהּ בָּנִים,
phrases.english: If she married the first and she did not have children,
the second and she did not have children,
she may not marry a third
except one who has children.
If she married one who has no children,
she leaves without a marriage contract payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִיסֵּת לָרִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא הָיוּ לָהּ בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a woman presumed unable to have children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After two childless marriages she may marry only a man who has children. If she marries a childless man, she is divorced without a כתובה.

steps.title: Can the first two husbands take back their כתובה money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the first husbands can reclaim the כתובה money once a third marriage is also childless.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was raised: If she married a third and had no children, can those first husbands claim back from her? Can they say to her: 'It is now clear that you were the cause'? Or perhaps she can say to them: 'Only now have I become weak'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about money. Now that a third marriage was also childless, can the first two husbands say she was always the problem and take back the כתובה they paid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides are given clearly. The husbands argue that three failures prove she was the cause all along, so their marriages were a mistake. She argues the problem started only now, as she got older and weaker, so she was not the cause back then.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the Sages)
The matter has been revealed (now it is clear)

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: נִישֵּׂאת לַשְּׁלִישִׁי וְלֹא הָיוּ לָהּ בָּנִים,
phrases.english: If she married a third and she did not have children,
what is the law: may those first ones claim from her?
phrases.notes: They want back the כתובה money they paid her when they divorced.

phrases.english: Can they say to her:
It has been revealed that it was you who caused it.
Or perhaps she can say to them:
It is only now that I have become weak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: נִישֵּׂאת לַשְּׁלִישִׁי וְלֹא הָיוּ לָהּ בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא by asking about the money owed in the earlier marriages.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a third childless marriage lets the earlier husbands reclaim the כתובה money they paid.

steps.title: She can say she only became weak now
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes it is reasonable that she can claim she only became weak now, so the earlier husbands cannot reclaim the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable that she can say to them: 'Only now have I become weak.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in her favor. She can claim the problem began only recently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third failure does not prove she was the cause back in her earlier marriages. Her claim that she weakened with age is believable. So the first husbands cannot take back what they paid.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable / it makes sense

steps.whatToRemember: The earlier husbands cannot reclaim the כתובה money, because she can say she only became weak now.

phrases.english: It is reasonable that she can say to them:
It is only now that I have become weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question from the step before.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She can claim she became weak only now, so the first husbands cannot reclaim the money.

steps.title: Can she claim her כתובה from the third husband after having children with a fourth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, after having children with a fourth husband, she can demand her כתובה from the third, since she lost it only because of the presumption.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was raised: If she married a fourth and had children, can she claim her כתובה from the third?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the opposite question. Now that she has had children, can she go back to the third husband and demand the כתובה she lost?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the ברייתא, she lost her כתובה from the third husband because she was presumed unable to have children. Having children with the fourth husband seems to prove that presumption wrong. So she might argue she is owed the money after all.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
If she married a fourth and she had children,
what is the law: may she claim from the third?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: נִישֵּׂאת לָרְבִיעִי וְהָיוּ לָהּ בָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question on the ברייתא, this time with her making the claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether having children with a fourth husband lets her claim the כתובה she lost from the third.

steps.title: Better for her to stay quiet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that she is better off not making the claim. The third husband could say he would never have divorced her had he known she could have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: We say to her: 'Your silence is better than your speech.' For he can say to her: 'I did not divorce you with this understanding.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא warns her not to make this claim. Her own argument could be turned against her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she argues that she could have children all along, the third husband can answer that he divorced her only because he thought she could not. That would make the גט a mistaken one. Then her divorce could be undone, and her marriage to the fourth husband would be in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: With this understanding / on this condition

steps.whatToRemember: She cannot safely claim the כתובה from the third husband. Her claim could make her גט look like a mistake and put her fourth marriage at risk.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying she would win the money. It is saying the claim backfires, because it could undo her divorce.

phrases.english: We say to her:
Your silence is better than your speech.
For he can say to her:
I did not divorce you with this understanding.
phrases.notes: He means he divorced her only because he thought she couldn't have children, so the גט was given by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the step before.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She should not make the claim. The third husband could argue the divorce was based on a mistake, which would endanger her divorce and her later marriage.

steps.title: רב פפא: we cannot stay silent about a void divorce
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא attacks the answer of Step 6. If the third husband could say he divorced her by mistake, the גט would be void and her later children ממזרים, whether or not she makes a claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: Even if she stays silent, can we stay silent? Then the divorce would turn out to be void, and her children would be ממזרים!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the last answer. If we accept that the third husband 'would never have divorced her,' that creates a far bigger problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said she should simply not claim her כתובה, so the third husband never gets to argue that the divorce was a mistake. רב פפא points out that if this argument is true, the גט is void no matter what she does. Then her marriage to the fourth husband was never valid, and her children from him are ממזרים. A real problem like that cannot be hidden just by her keeping quiet.

keyTerms.meaning: She is silent / we are silent
Children born from a forbidden union, such as from a married woman

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא is only arguing about money. His point is that the claim in Step 6 would make the whole divorce invalid, and that would affect the status of her children.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בית דין cannot accept a line of reasoning that would cancel a divorce, even if the parties stay quiet. The status of the children is at stake.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objects to this:
If she is silent,
are we silent?!
phrases.notes: 'We' means the בית דין. Even if she doesn't speak up, the court can't ignore the problem.

phrases.english: The bill of divorce would turn out to be void,
and her children would be mamzerim!
phrases.notes: These are her children from the fourth husband, born while she would still really be married to the third.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 6 that the third husband could say he would not have divorced her had he known
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that claim is valid, the divorce was a mistake and is void. Then her children from the fourth husband are ממזרים, regardless of whether she demands her כתובה.

steps.title: Rather, she only became healthy now
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives the correct approach. We say she was truly unable to have children before and only became healthy now. That keeps the divorce valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we say: it is only now that she became healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא replaces the rejected answer with a better explanation. The divorce was not a mistake, because back then she really could not have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she only recovered now, the third husband's assumption at the time of the divorce was correct, so the גט stands. Her children are not ממזרים. This also means she cannot get her כתובה back from the third husband, because she really was unable to have children while married to him.
steps.whatToRemember: A birth after an earlier childless marriage is explained as a new recovery. It does not reach back and undo the earlier divorce, so the גט stays valid and the children are not ממזרים.

phrases.english: Rather, we say:
it is only now that she became healthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem that Step 7 raised against Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reasoning with a new assumption that she recovered later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The third husband could argue that the divorce was a mistake
steps.terutzMaskana: She is assumed to have become healthy only now, so the divorce is valid and her children are not ממזרים

steps.title: When husband and wife blame each other, she is believed
steps.stepSummary: A new case. The husband says the childlessness is her fault and she says it is his. רבי אמי rules that she is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said it is from her and she said it is from him, רבי אמי said: in matters between him and her, she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related case. Each spouse blames the other for not having children, and רבי אמי rules for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question matters because if he cannot have children, she may claim her כתובה. רבי אמי says that on these private matters between the couple, her word is accepted. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: From her / from him (whose fault it is)
Private matters between him and her

phrases.english: He said: it is from her,
and she said: it is from him,
Rabbi Ami said:
In matters between him and her, she is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אָמַר מִינַּהּ, וְהִיא אָמְרָה מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related new case about who is to blame for childlessness
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the spouses blame each other for childlessness, the wife is believed

steps.title: What is the reason she is believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אמי believes the wife over the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אמי's ruling, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally each side's word would seem equally strong. So the גמרא wants to know what gives her the upper hand.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind Step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the wife's claim is believed over the husband's

steps.title: She can know; he cannot
steps.stepSummary: She is in a position to know whether his emission is effective, like an arrow. He cannot tell this about himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is certain whether it shoots like an arrow; he is not certain whether it shoots like an arrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the wife has knowledge the husband lacks, so her claim is the reliable one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being able to father children depends on whether his emission is forceful, which is described as 'shooting like an arrow.' She can sense this, but he cannot judge it about himself. So her claim is based on real knowledge, and his is only a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear to her; she knows for sure
Shoots like an arrow (an effective emission)

phrases.english: She is certain
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Either way it means she knows for sure.

phrases.english: whether it shoots like an arrow,
phrases.notes: This is about his emission: is it forceful enough to cause pregnancy?

phrases.english: he is not certain
whether it shoots like an arrow.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She has firsthand knowledge of whether his emission is effective, and he does not, so she is believed

steps.title: רבי אמי: marrying a second wife requires divorcing the first
steps.stepSummary: The husband offers to marry another woman to test himself. רבי אמי says that even so he must divorce his wife and pay her כתובה, since anyone who marries a second wife must do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says: I will go marry another woman and test myself, רבי אמי said: even in this case he must divorce her and pay the כתובה. For I say: anyone who marries a woman in addition to his wife must divorce her and pay the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The husband tries to avoid paying by proving himself with another wife. רבי אמי rejects this based on his general view about marrying a second wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband hopes to show he can have children, which would mean he does not owe the כתובה. רבי אמי says he cannot keep her while marrying another woman. In רבי אמי's view, anyone who takes an additional wife must free the first one and pay her כתובה. So the test does not save him from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: I will go and marry a woman
He must divorce her and give her the כתובה
One who marries a woman in addition to his wife

phrases.english: He said:
I will go and marry a woman
and test myself.
phrases.notes: He wants to see whether he can have children with someone else, to prove the problem isn't his.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Even in this case he must divorce her and give the ketubah.
For I say:
Whoever marries a woman in addition to his wife
must divorce her and give the ketubah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אִיהוּ: אֵיזִיל אִינְּסִיב אִיתְּתָא וְאֶיבְדּוֹק נַפְשַׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the case of Step 9 to the husband's counter-offer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who marries an additional wife must divorce his first wife and pay her כתובה, even when he only wants to test himself

steps.title: רבא: a man may marry several wives if he can support them
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבי אמי. A man may marry several women in addition to his wife, as long as he has the means to support them all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A man may marry several women in addition to his wife, provided that he has the means to support them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposing view to רבי אמי's general rule about marrying another wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said that taking another wife forces a divorce of the first. רבא says this is permitted, with one condition: he must be able to support every wife. By רבא's view, the husband in Step 12 could marry another woman without divorcing his first wife.

keyTerms.meaning: To support them (to provide for them)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי holds that marrying an additional wife requires divorcing the first and paying her כתובה. רבא holds that a man may marry several wives, as long as he can support them all.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹשֵׂא אָדָם כַּמָּה נָשִׁים עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: A man may marry several women in addition to his wife,
provided that he has the means to support them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: נוֹשֵׂא אָדָם כַּמָּה נָשִׁים עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אמי's general rule in Step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man may marry additional wives as long as he can support them all
